name: Deep ITM Call Stock Replacement
aliases: synthetic long via deep ITM call
summary: Replace 100 shares with a single deep in-the-money call at 0.85-0.95 delta, obtaining most of the directional exposure for a fraction of the capital with a defined floor.

legs.strike_rule: Deep ITM: strike such that call delta is in [0.85, 0.95], typically strike <= spot x 0.85; extrinsic value must be under 3% of spot

max_loss: The full debit paid, which is far less than the share notional — this is the whole point

greeks.theta: negative but small in absolute terms when extrinsic is minimal

when_to_use: When long delta-1 exposure is wanted but the shares would consume too much of a $50k account, and when IV rank < 35 so the small extrinsic is not overpriced. It is the Level-3-legal substitute for a synthetic long stock, and the router should prefer it whenever a synthetic-long signal fires.
typical_dte: 90-365 DTE; longer tenors amortise the extrinsic over more time
entry_rules: LEVEL 2 LEGAL and fully executable on Alpaca Level 3. No short legs, no assignment exposure, no uncovered anything. This is the recommended Level-3 replacement for synthetic-long-stock.
Strike chosen by DELTA: nearest listed strike with delta in [0.85, 0.95].
Extrinsic gate: (call_ask - max(0, spot - strike)) <= 0.03 x spot. If the extrinsic exceeds 3% of spot, the option is a leveraged vol bet, not a stock replacement.
IV rank < 35 at entry; above that, the extrinsic embedded in a long-dated ITM call is expensive.

No ex-dividend date concerns on the long side (long calls forgo dividends, which is already priced in) but note that a high-dividend underlying makes stock replacement systematically worse — require dividend yield < 2.0%.
Size: debit per unit <= 5% of equity ($2,500). Deep ITM calls are capital-efficient but still represent full share-notional directional exposure.
Underlying price >= $20, ADV >= 1,000,000, OI >= 250 at the chosen strike.
management_rules: Roll out to a further expiry when DTE falls below 60, paying no more than 1.5% of notional for the roll.
Take profit at +25% on the underlying's price (not on the option's percentage gain, which is leveraged and misleading).
Stop: close if the underlying falls more than 10% below entry spot, or if the call delta drops below 0.60 — at that point it is no longer a stock replacement, it is a losing directional option.
Do not sell calls against it without recognising that the result is a diagonal (see synthetic-covered-call-diagonal), which introduces a short leg and all of the assignment machinery.
exit_rules: No short legs, therefore no assignment risk.

MANDATORY: close the call by 15:00 ET on expiration day if ITM. Auto-exercise of a deep ITM call buys 100 shares at the strike, creating a $10,000+ share position overnight with no prior decision — for a $50k account that is a material and unintended capital commitment.
If the call is OTM at 15:40 ET on expiration day it may lapse, but by then the delta stop should have closed it far earlier.
Never hold a deep ITM long call into the final session on the assumption that it will be sold in time; set the close as a resting order.
assignment_risk: NONE — there are no short legs. The counterpart hazard is OCC auto-exercise of the long call at expiry if it finishes $0.01 or more ITM, which converts a $2,500 option into a $10,000 share position. The 15:00 ET expiry-day close rule exists specifically for this.
buying_power: The debit paid in full, typically 15-25% of the share notional. About $1,800 for a 0.90-delta call on a $100 underlying versus $10,000 for the shares.
liquidity_needs: Deep ITM calls quote wider than ATM; require bid-ask <= $0.15 or 2% of the option price, and OI >= 250. Long-dated deep ITM strikes on mid-caps frequently fail this.
common_mistakes: Choosing a strike by price rather than by delta and ending up with a 0.70-delta call that behaves nothing like stock. Paying a large extrinsic and calling it stock replacement. Letting it auto-exercise.
zero_dte_notes: A 0DTE deep ITM call is pure intrinsic facing certain auto-exercise; it is a share purchase with extra steps and extra fees.
